tip: The -ebil in gelebilirsin adds can or able to: gel (come) plus ebil plus ir plus sin means you are able to come.
The -mış in çıkmamış marks hearsay: she has apparently never gone abroad, something you did not witness yourself.
The passive lives inside the verb: duy (hear) plus ul gives duyuldu, it was heard, with no doer named.
Add -ınca to a verb for once or when: ısın (warm up) plus ınca gives ısınınca, once it warmed up.
The -meli in gitmeliyim means must or have to: git (go) plus meli plus yim, I must go.
katılmak (to agree with) takes the dative, so the person ends in -e: size katılıyorum, I agree with you.
rağmen means despite and needs the dative before it: olmasına rağmen, despite its being, so despite the cold.
For an unreal past pair -saydı with -mazdı: olsaydım, had I been, plus olmazdı, would not have happened.
O kadar with ki frames a result: so much that. O kadar çalıştım ki means I worked so much that my eyes are closing.
Repeat the verb as aorist-conditional then bare command for no matter how: çalışırsan çalış, however much you work.
With a negative verb, pek means not really rather than very: pek beğenmedi, did not really like it.
Ne with ne de means neither nor: Ne çay ne de kahve, neither tea nor coffee, and the verb itself stays positive.
Add -ken for while at the same time: yağ (fall or snow) plus arken gives yağarken, while it was snowing.
Bir yandan with öte yandan sets up two sides: on one hand the pay, on the other hand the hours.
For a real, likely condition use aorist plus -sa: kazan (win) plus ır plus sak gives Kazanırsak, if we win.
Keşke (if only) pairs with the -saydı past to voice a regret: Keşke çalışsaydım, I wish I had studied.
Verb plus -madan önce means before doing: Yatmadan önce, before going to bed, and the verb carries no tense.
Add -dığında to a verb for when it happened: yağdığında, when it snowed.
The causative -dır makes someone gain something: kazan (gain) plus dır gives kazandırmak, to make gain or instill.
The -alım ending makes a let us suggestion, here negative: unutmayalım, let us not forget.
ait (belonging to) takes the dative on the word before it: dönemine ait, belonging to the period.
